8671.overview:
Track & Field, known in Japan as Hyper Olympic, is a 1983 Olympic-themed arcade game developed and published by Konami. Events include the 100 meter dash, the hammer throw, the javelin throw, the long jump, the high jump and the 110 meter hurdles.

The arcade version was released in 1983. The simple gameplay, based on quick repeating button presses, set the basics for sequels and similar games in the genre for the next decades.

8724.overview: '88 Games (known as "Hyper Sports Special" in Japan) is the third instalment in Konami's '"Track & Field" series. As the name implies, the player is to compete into the 1988 Olympic Summer Games through eight events: 100m Dash, Long Jump, 400m Relay, Skeet Shooting, 110m Hurdles, Archery, Javelin Throw and High Jump. The goal is to qualify for every final through a first round of event, then to win the gold medal in each of them. '88 Games was released in July 1988 in Japan.

8731.overview:
Frogger is an action arcade game with single-player and alternating two-player modes. The objective is to guide frogs safely from the bottom of the screen to the home slots at the top. Each attempt requires crossing a busy multi-lane road filled with cars, trucks, and other vehicles, then navigating a hazardous river filled with moving logs, turtles, alligators, and other obstacles. A successful run places a frog into one of the home slots, and once all five are occupied, the player advances to the next, more difficult level. The game has no conventional ending, instead continuing through increasingly difficult levels until the player runs out of lives.

Movement is tile-based, with each input moving the frog one space up, down, left, or right. This makes timing and positioning equally important, as the frog must avoid traffic, line up with moving platforms, and reach the home slots precisely. Vehicles move horizontally across the road at varying speeds, and contact with any of them costs the frog a life. After crossing the road, the frog reaches a median strip before entering the river section, where the water itself is deadly. To cross, the frog must ride on moving logs, turtles, and other floating objects. Some turtles periodically dive beneath the surface, forcing careful timing. Later levels introduce additional hazards such as snakes, otters, and alligators, whose open mouths are dangerous to touch.

12200.overview:
Flying Shark, released in North America as Sky Shark, is a 1987 vertical scrolling shooter arcade game developed by Toaplan and published by Taito in Japan, Electrocoin in the United Kingdom, Model Racing in Italy, and Romstar in North America.

In 1989, the game received a sequel titled Zame! Zame! Zame!.

12269.overview:
Heated Barrel is a Western themed side-scrolling shoot 'em up game that supports up to four players at the same time. The game offers four typical Western characters to choose from: Howdy Pardner with his shotgun, the Mexican Chi Chi Gringo throwing boomerangs, the axe throwing Indian Little Plum and Billy Six Guns a revolver shooting guy. As you make progress you fight cowboys, Indians and ghosts.

While shooting in all directions you walk across towns, deserts and rivers blasting everything that crosses your path. Along the way, you can pick up several items, including power-ups that make your bullets stronger, a double star item that gives your character a second weapon, so you can shoot both at the same time, extra lives and a barrel, which you can use to blow up everything near you and makes you invincible for a brief amount of time, this is useful when you are surrounded. Some levels have large mid-bosses and all of them have an end-of-level boss.

12293.overview:
Hat Trick Hero '94 was produced by Taito in 1994.

A cool soccer game from Taito.

12955.overview:
Warriors of Fate is a 2D side-scrolling beat 'em-up and sequel to Dynasty Wars taking place in ancient China. Akkila-orkhan the dark lord of Shang-Lo has decided to conquer the neighboring countries. The wise Kuan-Ti has summoned the five greatest warriors of the lands to stop this from happening. The five warriors to choose from are(international names) Portor, Kassar, Subutai, Abaka and old man Kadan.

As you make progress you encounter numerous different enemies including spearman, archers, mace wielding soldiers, hand to hand fighters and bosses. Various weapons dropped by enemies can be picked up and used. Along the way health can be replenished by consuming food as well as mounting a horse. The game can be played solo or with up to two friends in the arcade version. The Saturn and PlayStation version allow two player to play.

15078.overview:
Heavy Barrel is a shooter with a top-down view similar to Commando and Ikari Warriors. Terrorists have seized the underground control complex of a nuclear missile site. It is up to the player to infiltrate the installation and eliminate the leader of the terrorist army before they can launch the missiles. To stop the terrorists you will need the powerful weapon Heavy Barrel. The problem is that the weapon still is in the installation. Before the fortress fell the weapon was taken apart and locked in six different storage lockers. To defeat the terrorists you must collect all keys and reassemble the weapon.

The name of the game is from an in-game weapon. The Heavy Barrel is found in six pieces and is an energy cannon capable of destroying any enemy in the game with a single shot (except the final enemy, and possibly one other boss that may have required two shots). The weapon has a wide arc of fire and can be fired as fast as the player's trigger finger permits, but after thirty seconds its use is exhausted, at which point the bearer reverts to his previous weaponry. Best used to get past tough bosses, the weapon could be built several times in a single game (probably three or four times). In a two-player game, whoever collects the sixth piece is equipped with the Heavy Barrel.

19732.overview: The House of the Dead is a first-person, light gun arcade game. Players assume the role of agents Thomas Rogan and "G" in their efforts to repel the dangerous, inhumane experiments of Dr. Curien, a madman.

24932.overview:
Hook is a side-scrolling, weapon based beat'em up, based on the movie with the same title. The player takes the role of a grown-up Peter Pan, whose kids have been kidnapped by Captain Hook. Tinker Bell takes Peter back to Neverland where he must again become Pan and reclaim his children.

The players must hack their way past Hook's denizens through 11 levels. These include forests, icy regions, and towns which Peter will have to jump, climb, and swim through. Magic items such as apples and pixie dust can be collected for special powers. When enemies are attacked, they simply put their hands up in surrender rather than dying, so as to make the game more child-friendly.

25585.overview:
Hard Hat is a unique logic game with an educational puzzle to solve. It was designed and programmed for Exidy by Larry W. Hutcherson Sr. and released in 1982. Touted as the “First Educational Coin-Op Game”, you play a busy carpenter that is constantly being chased by hammers and whirlwinds throughout a grid of scaffolding while manipulating letters to spell “E-X-I-D-Y” or “H-A-R-D-H-A-T”. Controls consist of a simple 4-direction joystick, both players alternating use during a two player game.

The hardware is identical to another Exidy game, Pepper II.

26044.overview:
Hyper Street Fighter II: The Anniversary Edition is a fighting game that ran on the same CP System II hardware as its predecessor and was the final game released for the platform.

Created to commemorate the 15th anniversary of the Street Fighter series, it is a modified port of Super Street Fighter II Turbo (1994) in which players can control any versions of the main characters from the five Street Fighter II games previously released for the arcades: The World Warrior, Turbo, Champion Edition, Super, and Super Turbo). This totals to 17 characters with 65 variations.

26302.overview:
Haunted Castle is a 2D arcade platform game, part of the Castlevania game universe. It's the first game in the series for arcade machines.

The game's main hero is once again Simon Belmont. He wants to rescue his wife Selena from Dracula. The gameplay is simple - Simon goes from left to right and fights against various enemies - skeletons, zombies, bats, and others. Belmont has his trusty whip and can carry one sub-weapon, like bombs. Hearts are ammo, required to use any type of sub-weapon The game has 6 levels, every one ending with a boss fight.

28657.overview: The House of The Dead 2 is a conversion of Sega's popular light gun arcade game. In this game, you play the role of a detective out to stop a madman who has unleashed zombies and other horrid creatures in an Italian city. You have to kill the monsters, save people and find out the plans behind this mayhem. The game uses an auto game camera that pans around in a preset manner as you venture through the city killing the creatures and rescuing people. Extra modes like training and time trial are included for replayability.

28762.overview: Demon's World, released in Japan as Horror Story , is a platformer arcade game that was developed by Toaplan and published by Taito in 1989. This game is multi-regional, meaning that it can be configured for different regions via the DIP switches. These settings change the legal warnings, can display the Taito licensing message and can change the title between the English version (Demon's World) and the Japanese version (Horror Story).

29453.overview: Boxing Game. You play the role of Jabbin Jim who fights his way through different opponnents each tougher than the last. Some of the opponents are recognisable from the Rocky movies. Your boxer has three attributes: strength, speed, and staminia, and these all contribute to his overall power rating. The attributes can be improved by taking part in mini games between the rounds.

29463.overview:
In the peaceful town of Carpentersville, some workers known as The Rusty Nailers decide to bulldoze a house that belongs to Harry. Harry is certainly not happy with this, and goes on a rampage, destroying workers that get in his way. As Harry, you can destroy workers in one of two ways: you can smash them when one of them gets near them, or you can pound the ground, and by doing this, you will send shockwaves in both directions. 

There are four environments in which Harry needs to get through: construction sites, sewer, ship, and the mansion where Harry meets the leader who ordered the demolition of his house. At the end of each environment, a boss needs to be defeated in order to proceed to the next environment. In between these, there are bonus stages in which you have to destroy a number of enemies before time runs out.

29466.overview: Hotdog Storm is a 2D arcade vertically scrolling shooter. The player controls spaceship and eliminates various enemies - mechas, helicopters, other spaceships etc. He has a basic cannon, limited supply of bombs, and collectable powerups.

31868.overview:
BurgerTime is a fixed-screen platform game in which the player controls chef Peter Pepper as he assembles several oversized hamburgers. Each kitchen consists of platforms and ladders covered by layers of buns, patties, lettuce, cheese, and tomatoes. The objective is to drop every ingredient onto the plates at the bottom of the screen.

Each ingredient is divided into several sections. Walking across every section causes the entire layer to fall to the platform below. A falling ingredient also knocks down any layer beneath it, potentially creating a chain reaction. Enemies standing on an ingredient when it falls are carried downward and may cause it to drop additional levels, while enemies caught underneath are crushed. Both methods provide considerably more points than simply completing a burger.

33565.overview: This is an updated version of Namco's "Pac-Man", featuring forced-perspective 3-D graphics that allow the players to jump over the enemy ghosts; in a similar fashion to Namco's "Pac-Mania", released in 1987. There are secret items and food to be found on each level that increases the player's power and score. For extra bonus stages, complete a level without eating any of the power dots.

34440.overview: Crypt Killer (known as Henry Explorers in Japan) is an arcade video game produced by Konami. It was then released in 1997 for the Sega Saturn and Sony PlayStation home consoles. The game was also released in Japan for the PC. The Saturn version made use of Sega's virtua gun which was developed for the Virtua Cop series of games. It was also compatible with the many lightguns produced for the PlayStation, namely the Konami Justifier. Scenery visuals and characters were all in 3D, while most of the enemies were in "flat" 2D sprites. Despite its horror theme the game doesn't take the theme seriously at all, relying on extensive gameplay instead due to its difficulty.

36585.overview:
A light-gun game in which three cops enter a haunted house to rescue a kidnapped girl. There are also secrets which add to the storyline.

This game plays like The House of the Dead, but it is different from that. Players one and three are equipped with pistols, which, when charged by pointing the barrel up, can fire more powerful penetrating bullets. This is best used for taking out a group of zombies. Player two is equipped with a shotgun which covers a wider range

Also known as Hell Night in Europe.

37124.overview:
Halley's Comet was produced by Taito in 1986.

Halley's comet is a space-based vertical shoot-em-up, where your spacecraft must defend each of the planets of the solar system (and the sun) from an incoming comet. Accompanying each comet is a wave of alien fighters. The fighters will cause damage to the planet you are defending if you let them past you. If you lose all of your ships, allow too many aliens to attack the planet, or take too long to destroy the comet, then the planet is lost and your game is over.

A comet is defeated in three stages. First, you must destroy aliens and then get past a guardian starship. Secondly, you must reach the comet's surface and shoot holes into the surface. Finally, you must invade the comet and take out the core. A display on the right of the screen shows the comet getting closer and closer to the planet, and the percentage damage done by aliens that were not intercepted.

Your ship starts out slow and with a single puny laser. But there are numerous power-ups which increase your speed, strengthens your main laser, adds spread fire, or add some small ships which fly behind you and supplement your weaponry. A fully upgraded ship packs a lot of firepower, but it is all lost if you run into something. Once all of the planets have been defended in turn, the game starts loops back to the beginning.

37139.overview: Don-chan Puzzle: Hanabi de Doon! is a rare, fireworks-themed falling-block puzzle arcade game released by Aruze in December 2003. Developed by Takumi Corporation, it runs on the Aleck 64 hardware (an arcade system board based on the Nintendo 64 architecture). The game features characters from Aruze's popular Hanabi series of pachislot machines, most notably its mascot Don-chan.

37148.overview:
Hang-On Jr. is a point-to-point 3D racing game in which players take control of a superbike and must race over five twisting, road-based circuits, avoiding rival bikers and trying to reach each end-of-stage checkpoint before the time limit expires.

The game is a cut-down version of its legendary parent, "Hang-On", and while it features similar gameplay, it's rendered in more primitive graphics due to the vastly inferior host hardware. As with the parent game, collisions with roadside objects will see the rider thrown from his bike as the bike then explodes, costing valuable seconds waiting for a replacement to appear. Contact with rival racers should also be avoided.

A new addition from Hang-On is the presence of water puddles on the road, which slow the rider down. Any time remaining when a checkpoint is reached is carried over to the next stage. The game consists of two sets of five identical stages. Completing the first set (Novice) unlocks the second set (Advanced).

37159.overview: A colorful 3D three-on-three street baketball game from Sega.

37163.overview: A one or two player shooting game with a prohibition-era mobster theme.  Italian company Playmark essentially hacked and reskinned TADCorp's Blood Bros.

37165.overview: You are the Sheikh of the Desert, and your 6-bed harem is looking empty. Take on the ultimate rescue mission across treacherous sands! Snatch odalisques from speeding jeeps, passing camels, and hidden tents, then race them back to safety. But watch out! Angry servants are on your tail, a nasty monkey is throwing monkey wrenches into your plans, and a deadly, fast pink snake is ready to strike! Can you survive the hazards and complete your harem?

37169.overview: Hat Trick is a two-on-two hockey game. Each player controls a goalie and a skater. The object is to shoot the puck into the opposing teams goal. Each game lasts two minutes.

37170.overview:
European Football Champ was released to coincide with the 1992 European Championships. The game scrolls horizontally at a slight angle, and recreates the coin-op's close-up zoom effect after a player scores. Only a small area of the pitch is on screen at a time, but there is a scanner to show the whole pitch.

Although the game has a referee, he often loses attention, and these moments give you a chance to foul, punch or side-swipe opposition players. One and two player options are included.

37171.overview:
Hat Trick Hero '95 was produced by Taito in 1994.

An updated version of the previous game (Hat Trick Hero '94)

37172.overview: Shoot the colors on the same colors of the screen. When three or more same colored blocks draw a line, they dissapear. By terminating all blocks, the stage is clear. After the 50th stage, the game is over.

37176.overview: Hayaoshi Quiz: Grand Champion Taikai is a Japanese quiz arcade game released in 1994 by the video game company Jaleco. The title roughly translates to "Fast-Buzz Quiz: Grand Champion Tournament."

37177.overview:
Hayaoshi Quiz Nettou Namahousou is a Japanese quiz arcade game released in 1994 by Jaleco. The game was built for the Jaleco Mega System 32 arcade hardware platform, which was known for handling advanced 2D sprite scaling and featuring high-quality audio driven by the Yamaha YMF271 sound chip.

The title translates roughly to "Fast-Finger Quiz: Fierce Live Broadcast Battle", framing the quiz game around a high-energy television studio broadcast theme. Players compete in trivia rounds using specialized arcade control panels typically outfitted with large "buzzer" buttons (hayaoshi buttons) to ring in quickly against opponents or the clock.

37178.overview:
Hayaoshi Quiz Ouza Ketteisen: The King Of Quiz (早押しクイズ ～王座決定戦～) is a Japanese arcade quiz game developed and published by Jaleco.

The title roughly translates to "Fast-Press Quiz: Throne Decision Match." True to its name, players must test their trivia knowledge and reflex speed to hit the buzzer and correctly answer questions before their opponents do.

37183.overview:
Heart Attack was produced by Century Electronics in 1983.

Fill the maze with dots. Drop a plug to block the enemy or freeze the enemy for five seconds. You must complete the maze before time runs out.

37200.overview:
Hero In The Castle Of Doom was developed by Seatongrove and licensed to Crown Vending in 1984.

The game featured (once again) Quasimodo’s attempts to rescue Esmeralda (or, in this case Ezzmerelda). This one is basically a rip-off of Tutankham (though not a blatant one). Interestingly, the original flyers for the game referred to it as Hero in the “Temple” of Doom and featured the image of an Indiana-Jones-like character, complete with fedora (one wonders if they changed the name and character in an effort to avoid litigation).

37211.overview:
Hidden Catch is a classic photo-puzzle arcade videogame franchise originally developed and published by South Korean company Eolith. Debuting in 1998, the game introduced a digital twist on the classic "spot the difference" puzzle game concept.

The series is well-remembered for its hardware gimmick: instead of using traditional joysticks or buttons, players used an attached interactive pen to click directly on the screen. The pens contained a built-in force-feedback motor that delivered a strong physical vibration whenever a mistake was made or a level failed.

37212.overview:
Hidden Catch 2 is a puzzle arcade video game developed and published by the South Korean company EOLITH in 1999. It is part of the popular Hidden Catch franchise, which specializes in "spot-the-difference" photo-hunting gameplay where players compare two images side-by-side to find discrepancies before time runs out.

The game features a colorful fantasy narrative where the "peace of Picture World" has been broken by a wicked wizard. Players guide "colour pencil knights" on an adventure to defeat the evil force.

37213.overview: 'Hidden Catch' is a directly experiencing puzzle game by comparing scenes on the left and right and finding non-matching parts with a pen. You can feel the fun with the powerful vibration generated from the pen, when you did not find 5 non-matching pictures or when you incorrectly found.

37214.overview: Hidden Catch 3 is a puzzle game developed and manufactured by South Korean arcade company Eolith and released in 2000.

37217.overview: High Impact Football is American football arcade game that was released by Williams Electronics in 1990; it runs on Midway Games's Y-Unit hardware (only with two DACs, instead of just one), features fifteen teams to select from (Atlanta, Miami, Africa, Chicago, New York, Oakland, Denver, Pittsburgh, Europa, Detroit, San Francisco, Cincinnati, Kansas, Texas, Vegas, Los Angeles, Washington DC and Buffalo), and allowed up to four players to play it simultaneously (1P and 2P play against 3P and 4P).

37220.overview:
High Seas Havoc, known in Japan as Captain Lang (キャプテン ラング Kyaputen Rangu) and in Europe as Capt'n Havoc, is a video game that was made for the Sega Mega Drive/Genesis by Data East. It was also released in the arcades running on a Sega Mega Drive/Genesis based arcade cabinet.

The story is about an anthropomorphic pirate seal named Havoc (Lang in the Japanese version), his young sidekick Tide (Land in the Japanese version), a girl named Bridget, and an evil pirate named Bernardo.[4] Bernardo is looking for Emeralda, a gem with powers that can cause whole armies to be toppled.[4] A map shows where Emeralda is located, and Bernardo is looking for the map.[4] Havoc and Tide discover Bridget unconscious at a beach.[4] When she wakes up in a dwelling, she instructs Havoc to keep her and the map safe.[4] Havoc hides the map in a cliff.[4] After Bernardo's henchmen kidnaps Bridget and Tide; Havoc, the playable character, sets off to rescue them.[4]

Each level apart from the first two and last one have two acts. The Cape Sealph level was removed from the European version

37240.overview: Hokuha Syourin Hiryū no Ken (北派少林 飛龍の拳, lit. "North Faction Shaolin - Fist of the Flying Dragon") is a historically significant 1985 arcade fighting game developed by Nihon Game (which later became Culture Brain). Released in Japan by Taito and internationally by Data East and Memetron under the title Shanghai Kid, it stands as the very first entry in the long-running Hiryū no Ken (Flying Dragon) franchise.

37246.overview:
Holosseum (ホロシアム) is a 1992 fighting arcade game developed and published by Sega. The name is a portmanteau of holography and colosseum, due to it being a fighting game created exclusively for Sega's hi-tech hologram theater cabinet, and is the second and last game created for it after Time Traveler. It was one of Sega's earliest attempts at creating a competitive fighting game along with Dark Edge, after the success of Capcom's Street Fighter II.

Holosseum plays similarly to other 2D versus fighting games during its release, which the player's character fights against his or her opponent in best two-out-of-three matches in a single player tournament mode with the computer or against another human player. The player has a character roster of four selectable fighters to choose from, each with their own fighting style and special techniques. Unlike most characters in Street Fighter II, these four characters lack fictional moves. In one player mode, after selecting a character, the arcade randomly selects an opponent. After the player knocks out the other three characters, the player will fight against the same character the player controls, followed by numerous extra fights against all four opponents randomly. Like Data East's Karate Champ, the amount of space to move around in Holosseum is very small.

37249.overview: Honey Doll is a adult puzzle game based on Dharma Dōjō. The objective is to clear the stage of all blocks on screen by matching identical blocks underneath the platform. The number of consecutive matching blocks you have to put together increases as the stages advance. Matching blocks of the same kind reveal letters that float to the top of the screen. Grab enough of these to spell "Go Honey" and you can play one of the three different bonus stages. Unlike Dharma Dōjō where only the leftmost block of the row could be knocked, in this game you can punch blocks from both sides. Clearing the stages reveal pictures of naked women (this feature can be turned off via a DIP switch setting).

37254.overview:
A horizontally scrolling shooter, Horizon is the spiritual sequel to Moon Patrol. Both were developed by Irem; Moon Patrol was licensed to Williams. There is no mention of Moon Patrol on the title screen as Williams still had the license at that time.

Players take control of a hover vehicle armed with a turret and a cannon, rolling over the terrain and alternating their position and perspective on three different lanes to destroy enemies and dodge attacks while avoiding obstacles and picking up fuel and other items.

Though never commercially released outside of Japan, it did at least make it to a location testing phase.

37257.overview: A Korean Puzzle Bobble/Bust-A-Move clone/knockoff by Pandora/Afega in 1998. There are two versions, one with adult themes, and one without

37260.overview: Hot Mind is a puzzle game developed by Playmark in 1995 for the Arcade.

37289.overview: Hyper Crash is a 3rd person perspective driving game where you have to drive along a course over various stages destroying as many cars as you can. As you drive along, a fuel gauge slowly decreases and if this empties then it is game over. To re-fuel your car you must destroy the other cars to keep it topped up. There are two ways to destroy them, either by repeatedly ramming a car until its damage meter fills or flip your car in the air to land on them. Flipping your car destroys the other cars in one go but this wastes fuel. As you progress other cars will flip in the air as well and if you are destroyed then it wastes fuel. Other obstacles to look out for are barrels which when hit destroys your car but you can ram other cars into them.

37290.overview:
In Hyper Duel, the player controls one of three "Buster Gears” pilots: Keith Spader, Lisa Rowling, or Dr. B. Lloyd, and must destroy alien forces.
Buster Gears look like normal spaceships but have two modes - spaceship and robot - with different fire modes. 

The ships can also acquire additional helper units by collecting either the T or G items. The weapon can be upgraded by collecting P items.

37346.overview:
International Cup '94 (also known in Japan as Hat Trick Hero '94) is a classic soccer arcade video game released by Taito Corporation in May 1994. Capitalising on the hype surrounding the 1994 FIFA World Cup, the game features fast-paced, action-heavy football gameplay typical of mid-90s arcades.

Features a linear campaign spanning 7 distinct difficulty levels. Players choose their international soccer team and face off against randomly selected global rivals.

38262.overview:
Mutant Fighter is a fighter game from Data East that originally debuted in the Arcades. The game includes various characters influenced by Ancient Greek mythology and its combat is more wrestling-oriented, with grapples, suplexes and Irish whips.

The game appeared in Arcades in 1991, with the name Mutant Fighter in the west and Death Brade in its native Japan. ('Brade' is thought to be a misspelling of 'Blade'.)

38546.overview:
Penguin Brothers was produced by Subsino in 2000.

A multi-screen platform game where the players controls two penguins (one blue, and the other pink) fighting against various enemies.

38923.overview:
Rack + Roll (Hex Pool in Japan) is a billiards game developed by Shinkai and manufactured by them in Japan. It was published under license to Status Games in North America.

A billiards game in which you have to get all the balls in the pockets. There is no opponent, instead you have to just get them all in the pockets, ending with the 8-ball. However, if you miss three times, the game is over.

38924.overview:
Rack 'Em Up is a Billiards/Pool arcade game developed by Konami in 1987 with two game types: 9-Ball or Rotation.

Also known in Japan as "The Hustler".

39344.overview:
The game is mainly a horizontal scrolling shoot-em-up, although some scenes scroll vertically too. Shooting enemies will reveal power-ups and continually shooting them will either change their type or reveal a special weapon. Different weapons are more effective than others when fighting the end bosses.

Originating in the arcades, Side Arms is a horizontally scrolling shoot ‘em up in which you control Lieutenant Henry (a second player can control Sergeant Sanders in some versions), armed with crude weaponry and protective jump-suits. They must save the earth from the mercenary invaders of Bozon. You must first reach Bozon’s territories, then wipe out its forces hidden in caverns and lurking in underground seas, before destroying the main invasion ship. Lots of extra weapons can be picked up, often with similar tokens to those in 1943 and some other Capcom titles. Most weapons can be shot either to the left or the right, giving you more range to launch attacks.

39440.overview: The player controls the titular sun goddess and intergalactic warrior Amaterasu, who wields a magical sword and shield to defeat enemies with energy beams, in order to capture prisoners who escaped from a distant planet. Amaterasu can shoot in all directions in a manner similar to Capcom's Commando. She starts off with a less powerful energy beam and can be easily killed in one hit, but a motorcycle grants her improved mobility and an extra hit point. The weapon and motorcycle can be upgraded with power-ups to become respectively more powerful and turn into a spaceship with more hit points. A limited supply of bombs are available to defeat enemies more easily. Each level ends with a boss enemy's spaceship, which when defeated will reveal its driver, a prisoner, for Amaterasu to capture.

39752.overview:
Super Free Kick was produced by HaesungHJ Corp. in 1988.

A Breakout style game with a soccer theme.

40441.overview:
Video Hustler was the first billiards themed releases from Konami. More widely known by the names Lil' Video Hustler and Hustler, this arcade title features an overheard view of a pool table, but curiously, there are no pool sticks. There is no theme music to Video Hustler, but there are a couple of distinctive sound effects. Coming out in 1981, Konami is both the developer and the publisher for all arcade versions of Video Hustler.

There were no known ports for Video Hustler until rights were purchased by Microsoft in 2010. An updated version of Video Hustler is now featured on Xbox Live, which is an online platform where gamers can access this title if they are verified Microsoft customers. Although very basic, Video Hustler served as the inspiration for a few copycat titles as well as more sophisticated billiards video games released in the 1980s and the 1990s. Up to two players can play Video Hustler simultaneously, but alternating turns must be taken.

Video Hustler is a very simplistic arcade game. Levels are called patterns, and a small white marker is used to determine the angle of each shot. The objective is to get a high score. Only the five highest scores on any Video Hustler arcade machine were recorded.

Using the left, right, up and down keys, you must move this marker so that your invisible pool stick can strike the white cue ball and hit the colored balls. The idea is to get as many balls into the holes in as few shots as possible. At the start of every stage, six colored balls are racked and placed in the middle of the table. If you scratch the cue ball, that is, knock it into the pocket, you will lose a turn.

Scoring is based on a couple of factors. Each colored ball is numbered from one to six. Depending on the number of turns that it takes for you to complete a level, you will receive points based on the number etched on the cue ball that is multiplied by the 'bonus.'

Additionally, each pocket is assigned a multiplier. These values can shift and change according to the number of colored balls left on the table as well as angle of the last shot taken. Players are able to control the speed that the white cue ball travels by moving the angle marker. Parallel and horizontal shots always move faster than shots taken at awkward angles. The speed of the cue ball can also be increased when you attempt to hit a colored ball that is close by.

133155.overview: A sport game where players must qualify across eleven olympic events. The game features 32-bit 3-D graphics, great sound, as well as voice. This arcade game is actually an optimized version of the Playstation game "International Track & Field" and it is a great modernization of Konami's original Track & Field game. World records are kept permanently.

135701.overview: Unreleased video game. Last prototype version from January 1992.

155532.overview:
Hammer Boy is an arcade game that plays like a cross between Kaboom! and Whac-A-Mole.

Armed with a big hammer, your job is to prevent the American Indians from reaching the tower behind your fort by hitting them on the head and putting out the fires that are thrown from the side. That's really it to the game -- new levels bring different backgrounds (battleship, castle and space base) with corresponding enemies (pirates, knights and aliens), but essentially the same gameplay.

155533.overview: Happy 6-in-1 (欢乐六合一) is a PGM arcade game that includes a text-based quiz game, a cooking game, a tile-based game and three playing card games.

155544.overview: Steering Champ (Handle Champ in Japan and South Korea) is a collection of car themed mini-games from Konami. The game could be described as Bishi Bashi on wheels

155549.overview:
Hashire Patrol Car (Run! Patrol Car) is a niche, Japanese arcade game released by Sega in 2001. Running on Sega's ST-V (Sega Titan Video) arcade hardware, it functions as a video-based kiddie ride and a ticket redemption game rather than a traditional racing simulator.

The gameplay focuses on a simplified highway chase to catch fleeing criminals. Reviewers and arcade archivists note that the mechanics are largely predetermined, operating similarly to a video-based crane or ticket redemption machine.

156899.overview:
Hammer Away is an unreleased Sega System 18 arcade vertical shoot-'em-up game developed by Santos and set to be published by Sega in 1991.

The game was featured at Amusement Machine Show 1991 but is not thought to have been seen since. One theory suggests that from a gameplay perspective, Hammer Away failed to keep pace with more recent competitors, most notably Seibu Kaihatsu's 1990 hit, Raiden.

A prototype has since been found.

172541.overview:
Animal Basket © 2005 Sammy Corp. Known in Japan as "Hustle Tamaire Kyousou".

"Tamaire" is a traditional basketball game played by elementary school students at Japanese sports festivals. Animal Basket's furry competitors compete for a single ball and the goal is tied behind another animal's back, increasing the challenge with this moving target.

192685.overview:
House of the Dead: Scarlet Dawn is the fifth arcade game in the House of the Dead series. It takes place in 2006, between the events of The House of the Dead 4 and The House of the Dead III. The game's story follows AMS agents Kate Green and Ryan Taylor who infiltrate Scarecrow Manor just as a horde of bioengineered creatures attack. From then on they have to fight their way to safety while exploring the mansion and uncovering who is behind the outbreak.

Like in previous games in the series, the player uses a gun controller to shoot enemies as they appear on the screen. Each creature has a weak spot that deals extra damage when hit. In addition to the monsters, there are also civilians that have to be avoided. The player also has to keep track of the partner who at any time might need to be rescued. Failure to do so before time runs out leads to a life penalty. A new feature to the series is the introduction of quick-time events in which the player needs to quickly shoot a specific target. Reloading is automatic but can also be done manually by pointing outside the screen.

In addition to the main machine gun, the player can choose two more items (shotgun, grenade, rocket launcher, etc.) ahead of each level. In the Japanese version, items are bought with coins which are awarded for successful actions such as critical shots, collectibles obtained and saved civilians while in the international versions items can be chosen freely. Another Japan-exclusive feature is the use of Aime cards. They are used for storing progress, keeping collected coins, completing achievements, checking high scores and taking part in national leaderboards. Part of the Aime functionality is also a level system where players earn experience for each stage completed and are rewarded with coins for every level up.

The game has two game modes: normal mode and master mode. The normal mode is for first time players and includes assistance events. The master mode is for advanced players and has stronger and faster enemies.

422156.overview:
Starwing Paradox is a multiplayer arcade game in which two teams of eight players each pilot giant humanoid mechs in a battle to control the playing field and assault the opposing team's base. The object of the game is to destroy the opposing team's core, which is protected by a barrier that can only be brought down by capturing three of the five neutral objectives, known as ports, on the map.

In addition to the standard flying, shooting and sword-fighting actions expected of mech combat, the players' mechs can enter a high-speed "Full Drive" mode to move between objectives in a matter of seconds. Prior to each game, players can customize their mechs with an assortment of weapons and head/body/limb models to suit their play style and role within the team. Players can save their mech setups to a user account maintained by Square Enix.

Starwing Paradox was developed and published by Square Enix with animation produced by Sunrise.

423109.overview: Dynamite Baseball 97 (ダイナマイトベースボール９７) is an arcade baseball game and sequel to Dynamite Baseball. It was released in South Korea as Hanguk Pro Yagu 98.

425720.overview:
Halo: Fireteam Raven is a sci-fi fixed-gun shooter developed by Play Mechanix (in conjunction with 343 Industries) and released by Raw Thrills for arcades on July 10, 2018.

It is the first arcade game based on the Halo series and features an enclosed sit-down cabinet with unique fixed force-feedback weapon controllers (similar to Jurassic Park Arcade).

Set during the events of Halo: Combat Evolved, Fireteam Raven has up to four players controlling the ODST squad of the same name (consisting of commander Ethan Graves, communications specialist Marcus Hudson, heavy weapons specialist Victor Ramos, and demolitions specialist Ava Lang) as they fight Covenant forces on the surface of Alpha Halo. In the two-player variant, only Ramos and Lang are playable.

The game was originally released as a deluxe four-player model (with two 65" 4K displays side-by-side, with two players using each display), and was later released as a standard two-player model (with only one display). In November 2022, it received a standing four-player model with an extra-large 85" display and all four players using unique light-gun controllers resembling the MA5B Assault Rifle.

All models have smartphone support with QR codes, allowing players to track their scores using the Halo Waypoint app.

447065.overview: Hyper Sports was remade in 2011, based on Konami's original Hyper Sports from 1984. The cabinet was only released in China.The game offers the player several different Olympic events for the player to choose from, inlcuding Ping-Pong, Hurdles, and Long Jump.

465891.overview: Honky Tonk is a classic video slot machine released by the prominent Australian gaming manufacturer Aristocrat Leisure in 2001.
